mission: Build a fractal Google Maps of law for Swiss Federal Supreme Court case law from 2000 onward plus user-imported corpora, beating simple semantic-map baselines in legal usefulness.

corpus.question: Build the smallest reproducible TF-2000+ acquisition/normalization slice and canonical decision schema. Investigate official TF access first; preserve a path to bulk scale and user corpus import.

legal-distance.question: Establish strong semantic-map baselines and test which legally structured signals improve nearest-neighbor legal relevance while suppressing procedural boilerplate.

fractal-map.question: Establish a flat-map baseline, then test hierarchical/multi-resolution representations where zoom reveals legally coherent substructure rather than merely magnifying points.

evaluation.question: Build evaluation using TF/Jurivoc or other human indexing where obtainable plus baseline-independent tests for neighbor relevance, boilerplate resistance, multilinguality and stability.

product.question: Build an ugly but real vertical slice: import/load corpus, compute/load map artifacts, navigate clusters/decisions, and keep architecture ready for TF base map plus user imports.

director_note: Broad methods allowed. No unrelated lanes. Prefer discriminating experiments and end-to-end product progress over speculative architecture.
